commands.text:
uv run xrpl-camp --help
uv run xrpl-camp self-check
uv run xrpl-camp start --dry-run < /dev/null

commands.step: Launcher smoke test (real download + checksum + exec)
Open PR if the report changed
commands.text:
if [ -z "$(git status --porcelain -- .github/freshness-report.md)" ]; then
  echo "Report content is unchanged since the last run -- nothing new to review, skipping PR."
  exit 0
fi

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

BRANCH="freshness-check/$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)"
git checkout -b "$BRANCH"
git add .github/freshness-report.md
git commit -m "chore: weekly freshness check ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%d))"
git push origin "$BRANCH"

gh pr create \
  --title "Freshness check: pin / dependency drift ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%d))" \
  --body-file .github/freshness-report.md \
  --base main \
  --head "$BRANCH"

VERSION=${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}
uv run pyinstaller --onefile --name "xrpl-camp" --console \
  --collect-submodules rich \
  --collect-data xrpl \
  xrpl_camp/__main__.py
OUTNAME="xrpl-camp-${VERSION}-${{ matrix.target }}${{ matrix.ext }}"
mv "dist/xrpl-camp${{ matrix.ext }}" "dist/${OUTNAME}"
echo "ASSET_NAME=${OUTNAME}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

commands.step: Verify PyPI actually serves this version

commands.text:
set -euo pipefail
IMAGE="ghcr.io/mcp-tool-shop-org/xrpl-camp:${{ github.ref_name }}"
EXPECTED="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
# Match the version line by NAME, not by position. `awk '{print $2}'`
# on raw stdout read the second word of the unmounted-/work warning
# and reported a failure against a perfectly good image.
LIVE=$(docker run --rm "$IMAGE" --version 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1 | awk '{print $2}')
if [ "$LIVE" != "$EXPECTED" ]; then
  echo "::error::Image reports ${LIVE}, tag claims ${EXPECTED}."
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: ${IMAGE} reports ${LIVE}."

commands.step: Check that GitHub Release and PyPI publish agree
commands.text:
echo "build-binaries: ${{ needs.build-binaries.result }}"
echo "github-release: ${{ needs.github-release.result }}"
echo "publish-pypi:   ${{ needs.publish-pypi.result }}"
echo "docker:         ${{ needs.docker.result }}"

if [ "${{ needs.github-release.result }}" = "success" ] && [ "${{ needs.publish-pypi.result }}" != "success" ]; then
  echo "::error::Release is INCONSISTENT for ${GITHUB_REF_NAME}: a GitHub Release was published, but publish-pypi did not succeed (result: ${{ needs.publish-pypi.result }}). PyPI does not have this release. Do not re-dispatch this workflow against the same tag -- check the Actions tab for an in-flight run first, then use 'Re-run failed jobs' rather than a fresh dispatch (see the concurrency comment near the top of this file)."
  exit 1
fi

echo "Release outcome is consistent (or nothing was expected to publish on this ref)."

set -euo pipefail
mkdir -p "$HOME/.npm-cli-sandbox"
npm install --prefix "$HOME/.npm-cli-sandbox" npm@latest
echo "$HOME/.npm-cli-sandbox/node_modules/.bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

commands.step: Confirm the npm in use can do OIDC
commands.text:
set -euo pipefail
NPM_VERSION="$(npm --version)"
echo "npm ${NPM_VERSION} / node $(node --version)"
# Fail here, loudly, rather than at the publish step where the
# symptom is a 404 that reads like "package not found".
MAJOR="${NPM_VERSION%%.*}"
REST="${NPM_VERSION#*.}"
MINOR="${REST%%.*}"
if [ "$MAJOR" -lt 11 ] || { [ "$MAJOR" -eq 11 ] && [ "$MINOR" -lt 5 ]; }; then
  echo "::error::npm ${NPM_VERSION} cannot negotiate OIDC; >= 11.5 required."
  exit 1
fi

commands.step: Verify the tag matches every version surface
commands.text:
set -euo pipefail
TAG="${{ github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}"
bash scripts/check-versions.sh
PKG=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
if [ "v${PKG}" != "$TAG" ]; then
  echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match package.json ${PKG}."
  exit 1
fi

commands.step: Wait for the release binaries this launcher will fetch
commands.text:
set -euo pipefail
TAG="${{ github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}"
# publish.yml builds three binaries + a checksums file onto the same
# tag. The launcher resolves them at runtime, so publishing npm first
# would advertise a version that cannot actually run.
for attempt in $(seq 1 40); do
  COUNT=$(gh release view "$TAG" --json assets \
    --jq '[.assets[] | select(.name | startswith("xrpl-camp-"))] | length' \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  if [ "${COUNT:-0}" -ge 3 ]; then
    echo "Release $TAG has $COUNT binaries. Proceeding."
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "Attempt ${attempt}/40: $TAG has ${COUNT:-0} binaries, waiting 30s..."
  sleep 30
done
echo "::error::Timed out waiting for $TAG binaries. npm was NOT published."
echo "::error::Check publish.yml -- npx would fail for anyone installing this version."
exit 1

commands.step: Publish to npm (OIDC trusted publishing, no token)
Verify npm actually serves this version
commands.text:
set -euo pipefail
TAG="${{ github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}"
EXPECTED="${TAG#v}"
# Same compensator as the PyPI side: a publish step can exit 0 while
# the registry does not reflect it. The five-month gap this repo
# carried was exactly that failure, unnoticed.
for attempt in $(seq 1 10); do
  LIVE=$(npm view "@mcptoolshop/xrpl-camp@${EXPECTED}" version 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ "$LIVE" = "$EXPECTED" ]; then
    echo "OK: npm serves @mcptoolshop/xrpl-camp@${LIVE}."
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "Attempt ${attempt}/10: npm does not serve ${EXPECTED} yet, waiting 15s..."
  sleep 15
done
echo "::error::npm publish exited 0 but the registry does not serve ${EXPECTED}."
exit 1
